timeline.body:
Clarify where to start troubleshooting on IllegalArgumentException by telling the field and index name.

Closes #89485

I need the following support from reviewers.

- Which is the preferred use of `name()`?
  1. Call it as many as necessary, as the overhead is ignorable.
  2. Combine them into `String name = name();`.
  3. Replace the second call with `it` or `the field`.
- How to kick off backport PR in a good manner after this PR? I will appreciate any reference/documentation.

Thanks.

timeline.body:
Hi @javanna Thank you for your support.

- test code: That's because I drafted https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/89485 as minimum as possible plus not to break anything carefully. But I've updated the test code as per your advice. :)
- backporting, etc: I appreciate it very much!
- changelog: I didn't know how things work. I see, I leave as it is.
- title: Your suggestion saves me because I couldn't find anything that meets the balance between descriptivity and length.
could you check why the index name is empty in the returned error? Is it a bug or is it due to the setup of the test?

reply.body:
Because the empty string is specified to `fullyQualifiedIndexName` here (line 42).
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/43e2852016fa28d2892324291c4de14bfc62fa73/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/index/fielddata/FieldDataContext.java#L33-L42
I think this happens only under unordinary situations like tests, as the use cases indicate.
can you provide a different fielddatacontext instance here and specify the index so that we can test that we get it back as part of the error?
I've pushed a change accordingly. Hope it meets the intention.

timeline.message: Replaced FieldDataContext instance with the one having a non-empty index name
timeline.author: Youhei Sakurai

timeline.body: super minor nit: could you remove the whitespace between Field and data? I've seen that that's how we refer to it in our docs and I would prefer to keep that consistent.
checkstyle complained about this line, not sure if you've already addressed it, but we have a hard limit of 140 characters per line. Can you double check?
